newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police arrest last of big Rio drugleaders.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police arrest last of big Rio drugleaders.

text.p: Brazilian police have arrested the last member of a list of wanted gangleaders who controlled drug distribution in Rio de Janeiro slums over the past decade, a public security spokesman said on Wednesday.

"This marks the end of a cycle," Milton Correa da Costa, spokesman for the state public security office, said of the arrest on Monday of Roberto da Silva, known as Robertinho de Lucas, in a bus station in Recife, northeastern Brazil.
At the time of his arrest, da Silva had been waiting for the arrival of his two children who were due to spend their summer holidays with him, local newspapers said.

Police announced last March that they had captured a man they identified as Robertinho de Lucas but the suspect turned out to be one of de Lucas' top men. Five other notorious gangleaders were arrested last year, one of whom was later found dead in his prison cell, strangled with his own shirt.
With minors now controlling drug distribution in shantytowns, police will concentrate on trying to reduce the age of criminal responsibility from 18 years to 14 years, da Costa said.
